content: {"summary":"CPU usage rose but the main issue was HikariCP pool exhaustion caused by the month‑end reconciliation batch; increasing maximumPoolSize mid‑incident is not recommended.","likely_cause":"Reconciliation batch parallelism (LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM) exceeds the pool size, causing all connections to be held and pending requests to grow.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CPU was elevated but never near its limit, indicating it was not the primary cause","evidence_ids":["RB-013#2"],"quote":"CPU on that pod was clearly elevated, around two thirds of its limit, but it never got close to the limit."},{"text":"The pool was full (20 connections) while pending requests climbed to ~40","evidence_ids":["RB-013#2"],"quote":"`hikaricp_connections_active` flat at 20, the full pool"},{"text":"Batch parallelism (24 workers) exceeded the pool of 20 connections, exhausting the pool","evidence_ids":["RB-013#5"],"quote":"more workers than the pool has connections"},{"text":"Operators chose not to raise maximumPoolSize and instead reduced parallelism","evidence_ids":["RB-013#6"],"quote":"We did not raise `maximumPoolSize`."},{"text":"Guidance advises throttling the batch and not touching the pool during such incidents","evidence_ids":["RB-013#7"],"quote":"throttle the batch; don't touch the pool."}],"next_checks":["Monitor hikaricp_connections_active and pending metrics","Verify current LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM setting","Assess CPU usage after reducing batch parallelism","Consider pool size changes only after batch completes"]}
